subject: Private deployment workload matrix and exception clarification
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: Alice Turner <alice.turner@oakridge-health.com>, Oakridge IT <it@oakridge-health.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment workload matrix and exception clarification

Team — attaching the initial workload matrix Oakridge asked for and a completed exception_request_form (PDF). Two asks: (1) confirm which components of our runtime we cannot support in their air-gapped/on-prem environment without a change request (I put probable blockers in column D of the spreadsheet), and (2) provide a high-level FTE estimate and timeline for the minimal on-prem path (pilot -> GA) so we can propose an exception lane to Legal/Revenue Ops.

Notes/background: Oakridge is evaluating a VPC + on-prem inference appliance combination. Their procurement lead (Alice) asked us to surface: expected infra footprint, compliance gaps (audit/tracing, KMS options), and the minimum Redwood team support needed for first 3 months after cutover. We need a firm recommendation by EOD Monday so sales can lock the procurement window.

Please review the workbook and flag any items you cannot sign off on. Karthik — can you highlight the perf-sensitive kernels and whether those need NVIDIA drivers not permitted in their environment? Grace — any immediate CS/ops asks for runbook/hand-off? Stephanie/Priyom — compile a minimal staffing & escalation rota that covers 24x7 MTL for the first 30 days.

Attachments: workload_matrix_v1.xlsx (XLSX), exception_request_form_filled.pdf (PDF)

Thanks — Marissa
Product Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: Alice Turner <alice.turner@oakridge-health.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment workload matrix and exception clarification

Marissa — reviewed the matrix. High-level technical callouts: 

- Kernel/drivers: the inference kernels we use for low-latency transformer execution require recent CUDA/cuDNN stacks on A100 or H100 for the performance targets indicated. If Oakridge's appliance is strictly CPU-only, we will need to either accept much higher tail latency or qualify a quantized CPU path (likely ~3-4x slower for 2k context workloads).

- Networked control plane: our current Private deployment assumes a lightweight control-plane callback for metrics/rollout control. If their security policy forbids outbound callbacks, we must provide a static offline control plane (adds ~2w effort to package and testing).

- KV cache persistence: to meet their cold-start SLA we recommend persistent KV cache on an NFS/attached volume; if that's not allowed, initial requests will have warm-up jitter for first 30–60s after bursts.

Estimate (minimal pilot): engineering uplift = 2 SREs (0.5 FTE each for 8 weeks), 1 infra engineer (1.0 FTE, 6 weeks), 1 runtime principal for architecture sign-off (0.2 FTE, 2 weeks). Risk: if they insist on non-GPU/airgapped, add 1-2 weeks for kernel fallback qualification and additional perf testing.

I'll annotate the spreadsheet with the kernel/drivers rows and mark the items that require a formal exception.

— Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: Alice Turner <alice.turner@oakridge-health.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2027 13:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment workload matrix and exception clarification

Adding ops perspective: 

- Runbooks/Hand-off: we will need a minimal runbook (deployment, rollback, emergency key rotation) and runbook walkthrough with Oakridge SREs prior to cutover. I estimate 2 half-day sessions plus 1 runbook authoring sprint (3 days, 1x Technical Writer + 0.5 SRE).

- On-call/Support: for the pilot we should offer a 24x7 escalation window for first 30 days with 1 primary on-call (SRE) and 1 backup. That maps to roughly 0.6 FTE across the SRE roster for the month. Include an explicit escalation play to Redwood engineering for perf regressions (P1).

- Security evidence: they requested brief evidence for audit/tracing (where logs are stored, KMS integration, and access controls). Karthik — can you confirm if we can provide sample audit logs without sending PII? Stephanie — legal will want explicit wording in the exception form about telemetry.

I'll draft a runbook checklist and drop into the Drive link once Karthik confirms the NFS/driver constraints.

— Grace
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
From: Alice Turner <alice.turner@oakridge-health.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 04 Oct 2027 09:16:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment workload matrix and exception clarification

Thanks — couple of clarifications from Oakridge side: 

1) On drivers: we do have NVIDIA GPUs on our appliance but firmware policy requires vendor-signed drivers only (no third-party kernel modules). Will that block any Redwood-specific optimizations?

2) For the control plane: outbound callbacks to Redwood's hosted endpoints are restricted but we can allow scheduled outbound syncs over a guarded egress proxy. Would a polling model (5m) be sufficient for rollout controls and basic telemetry?

3) On telemetry: we cannot send any raw request-level logs off-prem. We can share aggregated metrics and signed audit bundles when legally requested. What minimum telemetry do you need to support rollback/autoscales in the pilot?

Our procurement deadline is Wed EOD. If you can provide a short bulleted list of absolute blockers vs. recommended items, that would help legal make a decision on the exception path.

— Alice Turner
Head of IT, Oakridge Health
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Turner <alice.turner@oakridge-health.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, priyom_das@priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 04 Oct 2027 17:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment workload matrix and exception clarification

Appreciate the quick clarifications, Alice. Summary and next steps (action owners):

- Absolute blockers (need exception): 
  • Vendor-signed-only kernel modules: Karthik — confirm if any of our low-level kernels require unsigned modules or custom kernel patches. If yes, we must list as blocker. (owner: Karthik, ETA: Tue EOD)
  • No outbound telemetry at all: Grace/Karthik — confirm whether a 5-minute polled sync (aggregated metrics only) can meet rollback/autoscale requirements; if not, call out specifics. (owner: Grace/Karthik, ETA: Tue noon)

- Recommended but negotiable: persistent KV cache (better SLA), offline control-plane packaging (adds ~2w), and a one-week shadow run before cutover.

- Staffing ask (minimal pilot): 2 SREs (shared rotation, 0.6 FTE), 1 infra engineer (1.0 FTE) for packaging and testing, 0.2 FTE runtime principal for sign-off. Stephanie & Priyom — please convert to a named rota and cost estimate for Legal procurement. (owner: Stephanie/Priyom, ETA: Wed EOD)

- Deliverables for Wed: short bulleted blockers list for Legal (Marissa), annotated workbook (Karthik), runbook checklist draft (Grace), staffing rota & cost (Stephanie/Priyom).

If we can get those by Wed EOD we can propose the exception lane to Legal and proceed with procurement. Thanks everyone — I'll coordinate the legal summary once the items are in.

— Marissa
Product Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
